event: Nala holds the three sticks to the shrine lamp until their tips catch and glow red.
Thin grey smoke curls up from them, sweet and resinous.
She speaks calmly and clearly, so the crowd can hear.
"Old Grandfather of the Three Stones."
"Your people respect the old ways and honor their ancestors as they have for many years."
"May they be safe and prosper, that they may continue to do so for many more."
The smoke from the three sticks goes straight up in the still air, in three thin grey threads.
A murmur runs through the crowd. Someone near the front says, "Straight. Look. Straight up."
An old man at the side presses his hands together and bows his head. Then a woman. Then more.
Heads bow all through the crowd, a ripple of them, from the front to the back.
Somebody's grandmother is wiping her eyes with her sleeve.
The sharp-faced old woman has stopped watching Nala's feet and is frowning at the smoke instead.
She looks at Nala's shadow once more, long and ordinary on the ground in the lamplight.
Her mouth purses, and she says nothing, and she does not bow.
Beside Nala, Gu lets out his breath, very quietly, like a man setting down a heavy load.
The incense still burns in Nala's hand, the smoke still rising straight.
The two big broad-faced young men at the front can't hold still any longer.
"Honored spirit!" the bigger one calls out. "I'm Fang Da! This is my brother, Fang Er!"
"We heard about the beast in Zhao Jun's rice! When there's a hunt, take us! We're not afraid!"
"We'll stick it like a pig!" Fang Er shouts, and a few people laugh, and a few people hush him.
At the back, the weathered man with the bow shifts his weight, and watches, and says nothing.
